chunks: I advise you, O servants of Allah,
for it is the right of Allah over you, and that which obligates Allah to fulfill your right, and that you seek His help in it, and seek His help through it.
for piety is today the protection and the shield, and tomorrow the path to Paradise, its way is clear, its walker is the gainer, and its depositary is the guardian,

it has not ceased presenting itself to the nations past and present, due to their need for it tomorrow, when Allah will revive what He displayed, take back what He gave, and ask about what He bestowed.

How few are those who accepted it and bore it as it ought to be borne! They are the few in number, and they are the people corresponding to the description of Allah, Glorified is He, when He says: '...And very few of My servants are grateful.'

key_terms.الشَّكُورُ: The grateful; those who show gratitude for blessings.
key_terms.الْجُنَّة: Shield; protection from danger or punishment.
key_terms.الْحِرْز: Protection or fortress; a safeguard against harm.
key_terms.الْغَابِرِينَ: Those who remain or come after; the present and future generations.
key_terms.تَقْوَى: God-consciousness or piety; a state of awareness and fear of God that guides actions.

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Taqwa (piety) in this world and the Hereafter according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) exhorts the believers to cultivate Taqwa, framing it as the divine right over humanity that secures their right with Him, a concept central to Shia ethical theology as the bridge between worldly conduct and eschatological salvation. He highlights the rarity of true adherence to this virtue, linking the scarcity of the pious to the Quranic motif of the 'few' who attain spiritual success through gratitude and steadfastness.

en.sayed-ali-raza: [Advice about fear of Allāh and an account of this world and its people :] I advise you, O creature of Allāh,
that you should have fear of Allāh because it is a right of Allāh over you and it creates your right over Allāh, and that you should seek Allāh’s help in it, and its help in (meeting) Allāh.

Certainly, for today fear of Allāh is a protection and a shield, and for tomorrow (the Day of Judgement) it is the road to Paradise. Its way is clear and he who treads it is the gainer. Whoever holds it, guards it.

It has presented itself to the people who have already passed and to those coming from behind, because they will need it tomorrow (on the Day of Judgement) when Allāh will revive His creation again, take back what He has given and take account of what He has bestowed.

How few will be those who accept it and practice it as it ought to be practice. They will be very few in number, and they are the people who correspond to the description given by Allāh, the Glorified, when He says : “. . . And very few of My creatures are grateful!” (Qur’ān, 34:13)
